Demultiplex and trim tags and primers

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
demultiplex_and_trim_fasta.Rd

Demultiplex each input FASTA file using tag combinations located at the ends of merged reads, then trim primer sequences from the resulting reads.

The output sampleinfo.csv file is similar to the input fastainfo, but without the tag and primer columns.

Usage

demultiplex_and_trim_fasta(
  fastainfo,
  fasta_dir,
  outdir,
  cutadapt_path = NULL,
  vsearch_path = NULL,
  compress_method = "R",
  pigz_path = NULL,
  num_threads = 0,
  check_reverse = FALSE,
  tag_to_end = TRUE,
  primer_to_end = TRUE,
  cutadapt_error_rate = 0.1,
  cutadapt_minimum_length = 50,
  cutadapt_maximum_length = 500,
  sep = ",",
  compress = FALSE,
  quiet = T,
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

fastainfo

Data frame or path to a CSV file with the following columns: tag_fw, primer_fw, tag_rv, primer_rv, sample, sample_type (mock/negative/real), habitat (optional), replicate, fasta.

fasta_dir

Character string specifying the directory containing input FASTA files (listed in the fasta column of fastainfo).

outdir

Character string specifying the output directory.

cutadapt_path

Optional path to the cutadapt executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.cutadapt_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

vsearch_path

Optional path to the vsearch executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.vsearch_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

compress_method

Character or logical. Compression method: "pigz", "gzip", or "R". "pigz" requires pigz to be installed and available in the system PATH (or specified via pigz_path). "gzip" is available on Linux systems. "R" uses R.utils, which is cross-platform but slower. Relative speed: R.utils < gzip < pigz. Only needed if check_reverse = TRUE.

pigz_path

Optional path to the pigz executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.pigz_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

num_threads

Positive integer specifying the number of CPU threads to use. If 0, all available CPUs are used.

check_reverse

Logical. If TRUE, also check reverse-complemented sequences from the input FASTA files.

tag_to_end

Logical. If TRUE, tags are expected to be located at the extremities of reads (starting at the first base).

primer_to_end

Logical. If TRUE, primers are assumed to follow directly after tags (i.e., no heterogeneity spacer).

cutadapt_error_rate

Numeric value between 0 and 1 specifying the maximum allowed error rate between primers and reads (exact match is required for tags).

cutadapt_minimum_length

Positive integer specifying the minimum length of trimmed sequences.

cutadapt_maximum_length

Positive integer specifying the maximum length of trimmed sequences.

sep

Character string specifying the field separator used in input and output CSV files.

compress

Logical. If TRUE, compress output files using gzip.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppress informational messages and only display warnings or errors.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

Data frame corresponding to the output sampleinfo.csv file and one FASTA file per tag combination for each input FASTA file, containing trimmed reads.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fastainfo_df <- demultiplex_and_trim_fasta(
  fastainfo = fastainfo_df,
  fasta_dir = "data/fasta",
  outdir = "data/sorted",
  check_reverse = FALSE,
  tag_to_end = TRUE,
  primer_to_end = TRUE,
  cutadapt_minimum_length = 300,
  cutadapt_maximum_length = 350,
  sep = ","
)
} # }
